newsitem.title: USA: Tandem Q2 revs fall, currency a factor.
newsitem.headline: Tandem Q2 revs fall, currency a factor.

text.p: Tandem Computers Inc said that its second quarter revenues fell to $467 million from $470 million a year ago, due to a negative impact from currency.

Tandem reported second quarter net income of $26 million or $0.22 a share, compared with a loss of $49.6 million, or $0.42 a share, including a $52 million restructuring charge. Currency had a negative impact of 2.9 percent on revenues.
The company, which develops so-called "fault tolerant" computers that do not fail in emergencies, said demand for its high-end NonStop Himalaya K2000 Servers remained strong.
Sales of the mid-range K-series servers were up 22 percent from the year-ago period, Tandem said.
All geographical divisions reported quarterly revenues close to target, with 76 percent of its sales coming from Tandem's primary markets in telecommunications and finance.
Tandem said it continued to manage its business operations closely in the quarter, and as a result, it saw product profit margins improve 2.3 points to 58 percent of revenues.
Research and development and marketing, general and administrative expenses declined year over year, with MG&A expenses declining to $140 million, down $12 million.
Tandem also said it expects shipments of its new systems running Microsoft Corp's Windows NT software would rise significantly over the next two quarters.
Tandem further said its cash position improved signficantly, both quarter over quarter, and year over year, with a corresponding decline in its debt.

"Our transformation continues according to plan," said Roel Pieper, Tandem CEO, in a statement. "It is clear that our vision and strategy are on target and have returned Tandem to growth and profitability." Tandem also said it plans to launch a suite of NonStop Software products next month.
